verdict.rationale: Phaser documents installing from the npm registry with `npm install phaser`. A runtime probe confirms the package is live on npm (v4.2.1, MIT, ~263k weekly downloads), and it ships bundled TypeScript definitions and works with front-end frameworks like React and Vue, so it does act as an importable dependency. Nothing in the evidence covers tree-shaking or modular ES-module imports, and bundler integration is only implied by the framework and template support. Missing for 10: documented tree-shaking or modular imports, explicit bundler integration docs, independent hands-on corroboration of bundling and tree-shaking.

support.subject: As a web developer, the engine installs from a package registry into my existing toolchain — a library I import, bundle, and tree-shake like any dependency

citations.quote: Full TypeScript definitions can be found inside the types folder... modern editors such as VSCode will detect them automatically.
Phaser supports over 40 different front-end frameworks including React and Vue.
